findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_direct_usage, get_answering_line_offer, set_up_answering_line, get_line_messages, estimate_media_job, get_downloads · Private data: get_m2m_network, get_agent_services, get_sip_address, get_catalog, estimate_media_job, get_job, get_downloads, prepare_upload, unlock_job · Public sink: send_to_business, get_direct_usage, set_up_answering_line, get_sip_address, get_balance, prepare_upload, create_media_job · Destructive: get_receptionist_benchmark, prepare_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_direct_usage, get_answering_line_offer, set_up_answering_line, get_line_messages, estimate_media_job, get_downloads · Private data: get_m2m_network, get_agent_services, get_sip_address, get_catalog, estimate_media_job, get_job, get_downloads, prepare_upload, unlock_job · Public sink: send_to_business, get_direct_usage, set_up_answering_line, get_sip_address, get_balance, prepare_upload, create_media_job · Destructive: get_receptionist_benchmark, prepare_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "set_up_answering_line" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
